title: KCET 2026 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column D3 (revised per KEA revised key: Q40 marked grace)

questions.q: R-CH$_2$OH is converted into R-CHO by reacting with ______.
questions.explanation: PCC selectively oxidises a primary alcohol to an aldehyde without over-oxidising it to the carboxylic acid, unlike alkaline KMnO$_4$; LiAlH$_4$ and Na/C$_2$H$_5$OH are reducing agents, not oxidants.

questions.q: Glycerol is a trihydric alcohol. It contains ______.
options: One primary, one secondary and one tertiary alcoholic groups
Two primary and one secondary alcoholic groups
Two secondary and one primary alcoholic groups
One primary and two tertiary alcoholic groups
questions.explanation: Glycerol, CH$_2$OH-CHOH-CH$_2$OH, has two terminal primary -OH groups and one middle secondary -OH group.

questions.q: The correct IUPAC name of CH$_3$-C(CH$_3$)$_2$-O-C$_2$H$_5$ is
questions.explanation: The compound is (CH$_3$)$_3$C-O-C$_2$H$_5$; naming the longer chain (propane) with an ethoxy substituent at C2 gives 2-ethoxy-2-methylpropane.

questions.q: C$_4$H$_{10}$ undergoes: (i) (BH$_3$)$_2$ then H$_2$O$_2$/NaOH $\rightarrow$ P; (ii) P with CrO$_3$ (anhydrous medium) $\rightarrow$ Q; (iii) Q with CH$_3$MgBr then H$_3$O$^+$ $\rightarrow$ R + Mg(OH)Br. The organic compounds P, Q and R are
questions.explanation: Hydroboration-oxidation (anti-Markovnikov) gives the primary alcohol P (butan-1-ol); anhydrous CrO$_3$ stops oxidation at the aldehyde stage, giving Q (butanal); CH$_3$MgBr then adds to the aldehyde, and aqueous workup gives the secondary alcohol R.

questions.q:
Match the reagents in List - I with products obtained from their carbonyl compounds in List - II.
List - I: (a) NH$_2$OH (b) R-NH$_2$ (c) R-OH (d) H-C$\equiv$N
List - II: (i) Cyanohydrin (ii) Oxime (iii) Schiff base (iv) Acetal
options: a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i
a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - iii, b - ii, c - i, d - iv
a - i, b - iii, c - ii, d - iv
questions.explanation: NH$_2$OH gives an oxime, R-NH$_2$ gives a Schiff base (imine), R-OH gives an acetal, and HCN gives a cyanohydrin with carbonyl compounds.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde + Acetophenone $\xrightarrow{\text{OH}^-/293K}$ gives the major product 'A' via a base-catalysed condensation. [Options show drawn structures.]
options: Ph-CH=CH-Ph (a stilbene, with no carbonyl retained)
A benzene ring bearing both -CHO and -COCH$_3$ substituents (para-disubstituted)
Ph-CO-CH$_2$-C$_6$H$_4$-CHO (a ketone joined through -CH$_2$- to an aryl aldehyde)
Ph-CH=CH-CO-Ph (chalcone, formed by aldol condensation of the two carbonyls with loss of water)
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, so acetophenone's enolate attacks its carbonyl carbon (crossed Claisen-Schmidt condensation); dehydration gives the conjugated chalcone Ph-CH=CH-CO-Ph.

questions.q: Carboxylic acids are more acidic than phenols because
options: More resonance stabilisation of their conjugate base
questions.explanation: The carboxylate ion delocalises its negative charge equally over two equivalent oxygen atoms, giving greater resonance stabilisation than the phenoxide ion, making carboxylic acids more acidic.

questions.q: The compound that does not answer iodoform test is
questions.explanation: The iodoform test needs a CH$_3$CO- or CH$_3$CH(OH)- group; ethanoic acid (CH$_3$COOH) does not give a positive test, unlike ethanal, acetone and acetophenone.

questions.q: Nitration of aniline in strong acidic medium gives significant amount of m-nitroaniline because
options: In electrophilic substitution reaction, amino group is meta directing
In strong acidic medium, aniline is present as anilinium ion
-NH$_2$ group always directs to meta position
m-nitroaniline has higher molar mass than o&p nitroanilines
questions.explanation: In strongly acidic medium aniline is protonated to the anilinium ion, -NH$_3^+$, which is deactivating and meta-directing, so a significant fraction of nitration occurs at the meta position.

questions.q: Basic strength of alkylamines in aqueous phase is not decided by
questions.explanation: Basicity of amines in water depends on the interplay of inductive, steric and solvation effects; hyperconjugation is not a relevant factor here.

questions.q: The reaction sequence is: Benzene $\xrightarrow{\text{Conc.HNO}_3,\text{Conc.H}_2SO_4,323-333K}$ A $\xrightarrow{\text{Fe/HCl}}$ B $\xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl},273K}$ C $\xrightarrow{\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}}$ Benzene + D + HCl + N$_2$. Organic compound 'D' is
questions.explanation: Reduction of the benzenediazonium salt C with ethanol regenerates benzene (releasing N$_2$ and HCl) while ethanol itself is oxidised to ethanal, so D = CH$_3$CHO.

questions.q:
Statement I: Staggered conformation of ethane is more stable than the eclipsed conformation.
Statement II: The torsional strain in staggered conformation is more.
Read the above statements and choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: The staggered conformation is indeed more stable (Statement I true), but it has the least torsional strain, not more — the eclipsed conformation has greater torsional strain, so Statement II is false.

questions.q: From the given information, select the suitable law of chemical combination: Cupric Carbonate — Natural sample: 51.35% Cu, 9.74% C, 38.91% O; Synthetic sample: 51.35% Cu, 9.74% C, 38.91% O.
options: Gay Lussac's Law of Gaseous Volumes
questions.explanation: Since natural and synthetic samples of the same compound have identical elemental composition by mass, this illustrates the Law of Definite (Constant) Proportions.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct option (Based on mole concept):
List - I: (a) 2 moles of ethene (b) Molar mass is equal to 66 g (c) 1 g of H$_2$ (d) 2 moles of water vapours
List - II: (i) 11.2 L volume at STP (ii) 56 g (iii) 12.04 $\times$ 10$^{23}$ molecules (iv) 1.5 mole of CO$_2$
options: a - ii, b - iv, c - i, d - iii
a - iii, b - i, c - iv, d - ii
a - i, b - iv, c - ii, d - iii
a - ii, b - iii, c - i, d - iv
questions.explanation: 2 mol ethene weighs 56 g (a-ii); a molar mass of 66 g equals the mass of 1.5 mol CO$_2$ (44 g/mol) (b-iv); 1 g H$_2$ = 0.5 mol occupies 11.2 L at STP (c-i); 2 mol water vapour contains 12.04$\times$10$^{23}$ molecules (d-iii).

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II:
List - I (Element-Atomic number): (a) Ra - 88 (b) Ga - 31 (c) W - 74 (d) Pd - 46
List - II (Position in periodic table): (i) 4$^{th}$ period, 13$^{th}$ group (ii) 6$^{th}$ period, 6$^{th}$ group (iii) 5$^{th}$ period, 10$^{th}$ group (iv) 7$^{th}$ period, 2$^{nd}$ group
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: a - iv, b - i, c - ii, d - iii
a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - iv, b - ii, c - iii, d - i
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
questions.explanation: Ra (Z=88) is in period 7, group 2; Ga (Z=31) is in period 4, group 13; W (Z=74) is in period 6, group 6; Pd (Z=46) is in period 5, group 10 — matching a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

questions.q: The types of hybrid orbitals of nitrogen in NO$_2^+$, NO$_3^-$, and NH$_4^+$ respectively are
questions.explanation: NO$_2^+$ is linear (sp), NO$_3^-$ is trigonal planar (sp$^2$) and NH$_4^+$ is tetrahedral (sp$^3$), which would give order sp, sp$^2$, sp$^3$ (option A); the KEA key for this version marks option B — the key's answer is retained here (as per KEA key).
questions.note: The standard answer is (A) sp, sp$^2$, sp$^3$ for NO$_2^+$, NO$_3^-$ and NH$_4^+$ respectively; option (B), which swaps NO$_3^-$ and NH$_4^+$ to sp$^3$ then sp$^2$, does not match their known geometries.

questions.q:
In which of the following option/options, the order of arrangement does not agree with the variation of property indicated against it?
(a) BF$_3$ > NF$_3$ > NH$_3$ (Dipole moment)
(b) HgCl$_2$ > NH$_4^+$ > SF$_4$ (Bond angle)
(c) NH$_3$ < H$_2$O < HF (Strength of intermolecular hydrogen bonding)
(d) H - I > H - Br > H - Cl (Bond length)
questions.explanation: Actual dipole moments increase as BF$_3$(0) < NF$_3$ < NH$_3$, so (a) is reversed and disagrees; (b), (c) and (d) correctly represent the bond-angle, H-bond strength and bond-length trends.

questions.q:
With respect to resonance structures of CO$_3^{2-}$ ion, which of the following statements are correct?
(a) All C-O bonds in CO$_3^{2-}$ are equivalent
(b) There are three resonance structures possible for CO$_3^{2-}$ ion
(c) The position of carbon and oxygen should change in every resonance structure
(d) The formal charge on carbon atom is -2
questions.explanation: CO$_3^{2-}$ has three equivalent resonance structures giving equal C-O bond lengths (a, b true); only the double-bond position shifts among the oxygens, carbon's position is fixed (c false); the formal charge on carbon is 0, not -2 (d false).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements.
Statement I : In H$_2$O$_2$, each oxygen atom is assigned an oxidation number of -1, In RbO$_2$, each oxygen atom is assigned an oxidation number of -$\dfrac{1}{2}$.
Statement II : Representation of HAuCl$_4$ and MnO$_2$ in stock notation is HAu(III)Cl$_4$ and Mn(II)O$_2$, respectively.
Examine the above statements and choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: H$_2$O$_2$ is a peroxide (O = -1) and RbO$_2$ is a superoxide (O = -1/2), so Statement I is correct. In HAuCl$_4$, Au is +3 (correct), but in MnO$_2$, Mn is +4, not +2, so Statement II is incorrect.

questions.q: a C$_2$O$_4^{2-}$ + b MnO$_4^-$ + c H$^+$ $\rightarrow$ x Mn$^{2+}$ + y H$_2$O + z CO$_2$. a and x respectively are
questions.explanation: Each C$_2$O$_4^{2-}$ loses 2 electrons and each MnO$_4^-$ gains 5 electrons; balancing electrons needs 5 oxalate and 2 permanganate ions, so a = 5 and x = 2.

questions.q: Which of the following will not act as an oxidising agent?
questions.explanation: Down group 6, the stability of the highest (+6) oxidation state increases (Cr < Mo < W), so MoO$_3$ is a much weaker oxidising agent compared to the Cr(VI) species.

questions.q: The highest oxidation state of manganese in fluoride is +4 (MnF$_4$), but the highest oxidation state in oxides is +7 (Mn$_2$O$_7$), because
options: Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen
In covalent compounds, fluorine can form single bond only, while oxygen forms double bond
questions.explanation: Oxygen can form multiple (p$\pi$-d$\pi$) bonds with the metal, stabilising very high oxidation states, whereas fluorine (despite its higher electronegativity) can only form single bonds, so it cannot stabilise oxidation states as high as oxygen does.

questions.q: The calculated spin only magnetic moment of Cr$^{2+}$ ion is
questions.explanation: Cr$^{2+}$ has a 3d$^4$ configuration with 4 unpaired electrons, so $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{4\times 6} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ BM.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most stable complex?
questions.explanation: Oxalate is a bidentate chelating ligand, and chelation (forming multiple stable rings) gives [Fe(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$]$^{3-}$ exceptional stability compared to the other listed complexes.

questions.q: How many ions per molecule are produced from the complex [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]Cl$_3$ in solution?
questions.explanation: [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]Cl$_3$ ionises as [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ + 3Cl$^-$, which gives 4 ions in total (option B); the KEA key for this version marks option C (3 ions) — the key's answer is retained here (as per KEA key).
questions.note: The standard answer is (B) 4 ions: [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]Cl$_3$ dissociates into one [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ complex ion and 3 Cl$^-$ ions, totalling 4 ions per formula unit, not 3.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The M - C $\sigma$ bond is formed by the donation of lone pair of electrons on the carbonyl carbon into a vacant d-orbital of the metal
Statement II: The M - C $\pi$ bond is formed by the donation of a pair of electrons from a filled d-orbital of metal into the vacant antibonding $\pi^*$ orbital of carbon monoxide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: This is the standard synergic bonding description in metal carbonyls: a $\sigma$-donation from carbon to metal plus $\pi$-back-donation from metal to CO's $\pi^*$ orbital — both statements are correct.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II
List - I (Complex): (a) [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ (b) [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ (c) [Ni(CN)$_4$]$^{2-}$ (d) [Fe(CO)$_5$]
List - II (Geometry): (i) Trigonal bipyramidal (ii) Octahedral (iii) Tetrahedral (iv) Square planar
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i
a - ii, b - i, c - iii, d - iv
a - iii, b - ii, c - iv, d - i
a - i, b - iii, c - iv, d - ii
questions.explanation: [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ is octahedral, [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ is tetrahedral, [Ni(CN)$_4$]$^{2-}$ is square planar, and [Fe(CO)$_5$] is trigonal bipyramidal.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II
List - I (Vitamins): (a) B$_1$ (b) B$_2$ (c) B$_6$ (d) B$_{12}$
List - II (Deficiency Diseases): (i) Convulsions (ii) RBC deficiency in haemoglobin (iii) Retarded growth (iv) Burning sensation of the skin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: a - ii, b - iv, c - iii, d - i
a - iii, b - iv, c - i, d - ii
a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - iv, b - iii, c - ii, d - i
questions.explanation: B$_1$ (thiamine) deficiency (beri-beri) is linked to retarded growth, B$_2$ (riboflavin) deficiency to a burning sensation of the skin, B$_6$ (pyridoxine) deficiency to convulsions, and B$_{12}$ deficiency to reduced haemoglobin/RBC formation (pernicious anaemia).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: All monosaccharides are reducing sugars.
Statement II: Sucrose can reduce ammoniacal silver nitrate solution.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Every monosaccharide has a free (or potentially free) anomeric carbon, so all are reducing sugars (Statement I true); sucrose has no free anomeric carbon, so it cannot reduce Tollens' reagent (Statement II false).

questions.q: Incorrect statement about $\alpha$-amino acids of proteins among the following is
options: Methionine is an essential amino acid
Zwitterion of valine exhibits amphoteric behaviour
questions.explanation: Glycylalanylglutamine (Gly-Ala-Gln) is a tripeptide with only two peptide (amide) linkages between its three residues, so the claim of three amide linkages is incorrect; the statements about methionine, glycine and valine's zwitterion are all true.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II and select the correct options
List - I (Functional group): (a) Secondary Alcohol (b) C$_6$H$_5$NH$_2$ (Aniline) (c) CH$_3$CH$_2$CHO (Propanal) (d) Phenol
List - II (Functional group reagent): (i) Neutral ferric chloride test (ii) Azo dye test (iii) Ceric ammonium nitrate test (iv) Tollen's reagent test
Codes:
options: a - iv, b - i, c - ii, d - iii
a - iii, b - ii, c - iv, d - i
a - iii, b - ii, c - i, d - iv
a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: A secondary alcohol gives a positive ceric ammonium nitrate test, aniline gives the azo dye test, propanal (an aldehyde) reduces Tollens' reagent, and phenol gives a colour with neutral FeCl$_3$.

questions.q: When salt BA is treated with Conc. H$_2$SO$_4$, reddish brown gas is liberated. The aqueous solution of BA gives pale yellow precipitate with AgNO$_3$ solution. Which of the following anion(A) is present in the salt BA?
questions.explanation: Conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ oxidises bromide to reddish-brown Br$_2$ vapour, and Br$^-$ forms a pale yellow precipitate (AgBr) with AgNO$_3$, identifying the anion as Br$^-$.

questions.q: Which of the following represents de Broglie equation?
questions.explanation: The de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = h/mv = h/p$, matching option B.

questions.q: Which of the following is the CORRECT statement about $\Psi^2$?
options: Probability density of the electron at that point
questions.explanation: $\Psi^2$ gives the probability density of finding the electron at a given point in space; at nodes $\Psi^2 = 0$.

questions.q:
A: Entropy of a perfect crystalline solid at absolute zero approaches zero.
B: For spontaneity of a reaction, T$\Delta$S > $\Delta$H.
Among the two statements given above, identify the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement A is the third law of thermodynamics (true); for spontaneity $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S < 0$, i.e. $T\Delta S > \Delta H$, so B is also true.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct statement for a thermodynamic system?
options: The internal energy changes in all processes
Internal energy and entropy are state functions
The work done in an adiabatic process is always zero
questions.explanation: Internal energy and entropy are both state functions (path-independent); work and heat are path functions, and adiabatic work need not be zero.

questions.q: A gas can be taken from A to B via two different paths ACB and ADB. When path ACB is used, 60J of heat flows into the system and 30J of work is done by the system. If path ADB is used, work done by the system is 10J. The heat flow into the system in path ADB is [P-V diagram: rectangle with A at bottom-left, C at top-left, B at top-right, D at bottom-right]
questions.explanation: $\Delta U$ is path-independent: along ACB, $\Delta U = q - w = 60 - 30 = 30$ J. Along ADB, $q = \Delta U + w = 30 + 10 = 40$ J.

questions.q: For the reversible reaction, N$_{2(g)}$ + 3H$_{2(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ 2NH$_{3(g)}$. When the partial pressure is measured in atmosphere, the value of $K_p$ at 500$^\circ$C is $1.44 \times 10^{-5}$. The value of $K_c$ when the concentration is expressed in mol L$^{-1}$ is:
questions.explanation: $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$ with $\Delta n = 2-4=-2$; using T = 773 K (500$^\circ$C) and R = 0.082, $K_c = K_p(RT)^{2} = \dfrac{1.44\times10^{-5}}{(0.082\times773)^{-2}}$.

questions.q: For the following gaseous reversible reaction: 3A$_{(g)}$ + B$_{(g)}$ $\rightleftharpoons$ A$_3$B$_{(g)}$ ($\Delta H$ = -q kJ), the amount of product A$_3$B$_{(g)}$ is affected by
questions.explanation: The reaction is exothermic (temperature affects the equilibrium position) and involves a decrease in gas moles (4 to 1), so pressure also shifts the equilibrium; a catalyst affects only the rate, not the equilibrium amount.

questions.q: A 0.15 mole of pyridinium chloride has been added to 500 cm$^3$ of 0.2M pyridine solution (a base). Assuming there is no change in volume upon mixing, the pH of the resulting solution is (Note: K$_b$ for pyridine is $1.5 \times 10^{-9}$)
questions.explanation: This pyridine/pyridinium buffer has moles base = 0.5 L $\times$ 0.2 M = 0.1 mol and moles salt = 0.15 mol; pOH = pK$_b$ + log(salt/base) = 8.82 + log(1.5) $\approx$ 9, so pH $\approx$ 5. KEA awarded grace marks for this question in the revised key.

questions.q: Which of the following is CORRECT with respect to the property mentioned against it?
options: Osmotic pressure at 298K : 0.1M NaCl solution < 0.1M Urea solution
Concentration of NaCl in the solution : 2ppm > 2M
Vapour pressure at 298K : Salt water < Pure water
questions.explanation: Dissolving a non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure (Raoult's law), so salt water has a lower vapour pressure than pure water; the other three statements are each reversed from the true relationship.

questions.q:
Match List - I (Laws) with the List - II (Mathematical expressions):
List - I: (a) Henry's law (b) Raoult's law (c) First law of thermodynamics (d) Kohlrausch's law
List - II: (i) $P_1 = x_1P_1^0$ (ii) $p = K_Hx$ (iii) $\Lambda_m^0 = \nu_+\lambda_+^0 + \nu_-\lambda_-^0$ (iv) $\Delta U = q + w$
Codes:
options: a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - ii, b - i, c - iii, d - iv
a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
a - i, b - ii, c - iv, d - iii
questions.explanation: Henry's law is $p=K_Hx$ (ii), Raoult's law is $P_1=x_1P_1^0$ (i), the first law is $\Delta U=q+w$ (iv), and Kohlrausch's law is $\Lambda_m^0=\nu_+\lambda_+^0+\nu_-\lambda_-^0$ (iii).

questions.q: When 0.0106 mole of acetic acid was dissolved in 1 kg of water, the freezing point depression for this strength of acid was 0.0205 K. If the calculated freezing point depression is 0.0197 K, Van't Hoff factor (i) and degree of dissociation of acetic acid respectively are
questions.explanation: $i = \Delta T_{f,observed}/\Delta T_{f,calculated} = 0.0205/0.0197 \approx 1.041$; for HA $\rightleftharpoons$ H$^+$+A$^-$, $i = 1+\alpha$, so $\alpha = 0.041$.

questions.q: The relative lowering of vapour pressure produced by dissolving 18 g of urea (Molar mass = 60 g mol$^{-1}$) in 100 g of water is
questions.explanation: Moles urea = 18/60 = 0.3; moles water = 100/18 $\approx$ 5.56; relative lowering of vapour pressure = mole fraction of solute = 0.3/(0.3+5.56) $\approx$ 0.05.

questions.q: During the electrolysis of acidified water, 16 g of O$_2$ gas is formed at anode. The volume of H$_2$ gas liberated at cathode under STP conditions is
questions.explanation: 0.5 mol O$_2$ (16 g) requires 4$\times$0.5 = 2 mol electrons (O$_2$ formation needs 4 e$^-$); these 2 mol electrons liberate 2/2 = 1 mol H$_2$ (2 e$^-$ per H$_2$), i.e. 22.4 L at STP.

questions.q: $\Lambda_m^o(NH_4OH)$ is equal to
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch's law, the limiting molar conductivity of the weak electrolyte NH$_4$OH can be obtained from those of strong electrolytes: $\Lambda_m^o(NH_4Cl) + \Lambda_m^o(NaOH) - \Lambda_m^o(NaCl)$.

questions.q:
Given below are the half-cell reactions:
Mn$^{2+}$ + 2e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Mn (E$^\circ$ = -1.18 V)
Mn$^{3+}$ + e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Mn$^{2+}$ (E$^\circ$ = +1.51 V)
The E$^\circ_{cell}$ for 3Mn$^{2+}$ $\rightarrow$ Mn + 2Mn$^{3+}$ will be ______
options: - 2.69 V, the reaction will not occur (Non-Spontaneous)
- 0.33 V, the reaction will not occur (Non-Spontaneous)
questions.explanation: E$^\circ_{cell}$ = E$^\circ_{cathode}$ - E$^\circ_{anode}$ = (-1.18) - (+1.51) = -2.69 V; a negative E$^\circ_{cell}$ means the disproportionation is non-spontaneous.

questions.q: The conductivity of centimolar solution of KCl at 298 K is 0.021 Ohm$^{-1}$ cm$^{-1}$ and the resistance of the cell containing the solution at 298 K is 60 $\Omega$. The value of cell constant (G*) is
questions.explanation: Cell constant $G^* = \kappa \times R = 0.021 \times 60 = 1.26$ cm$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Which one of the following graphs is not applicable for a 1st order reaction (R $\rightarrow$ P)?
options: A graph of [R] vs t with a downward sloping curve.
A graph of ln[R] vs t with a downward sloping straight line.
A graph of log$_{10}$[R] vs t with an upward sloping straight line.
A graph of log$_{10}$([R]$_0$/[R]) vs t with an upward sloping straight line through the origin.
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, log$_{10}$[R] decreases linearly with time (downward sloping), not upward, so option (C) is the description that is not applicable; KEA's key for this version instead marks option (A) — the key's answer is retained here (as per KEA key).
questions.note: The standard answer is (C): log$_{10}$[R] vs t must slope downward for a first-order reaction, so that graph (upward-sloping) is the one that is not applicable; option (A), [R] vs t as a downward curve, is a correct first-order graph, not the exception.

questions.q: For a reaction having three steps, the overall rate constant is K = $\dfrac{k_1k_3}{k_2}$. The values of E$_{a1}$, E$_{a2}$, and E$_{a3}$ (activation energies stepwise) are 40, 50 and 60 kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. Then the overall E$_a$ (activation energy) of the reaction is
questions.explanation: Since $K=k_1k_3/k_2$, the Arrhenius exponents add as $E_a = E_{a1}+E_{a3}-E_{a2} = 40+60-50 = 50$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (option C); KEA's key for this version instead marks option (A) — the key's answer is retained here (as per KEA key).
questions.note: The standard answer is (C) 50 kJ mol$^{-1}$, from $E_a = E_{a1}+E_{a3}-E_{a2} = 40+60-50$; option (A) 30 kJ mol$^{-1}$ does not follow from the given activation energies.

questions.q: For a 1st order change R $\rightarrow$ P, the concentration of Reactant R changes from 0.1 M to 0.025 M in 40 minutes. The rate of reaction when the concentration of R is 0.01 M is
The activation energy for the reaction X $\rightarrow$ Y is 150 kJ mol$^{-1}$. The change in enthalpy for the above reaction is -135 kJ mol$^{-1}$. Then the activation energy for Y $\rightarrow$ X is
questions.explanation: E$_a$(reverse) = E$_a$(forward) - $\Delta H$ = 150 - (-135) = 285 kJ mol$^{-1}$.

questions.q: The intermediates in heteropolar reactions are
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Heteropolar (heterolytic) bond cleavage generates ionic intermediates — both cations and anions — unlike homopolar (homolytic) cleavage, which gives free radicals.

questions.q:
Statement I: Nitrogen in pyridine cannot be estimated by Kjeldahl's method
Statement II: Nitrogen in pyridine changes to ammonium sulphate when heated with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$ in Kjeldahl's method.
Read the above given statements and choose the correct answer from the given options.
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in the pyridine ring is not converted to ammonium sulphate on heating with conc. H$_2$SO$_4$, so Kjeldahl's method fails for it — Statement I is true, Statement II is false.

questions.q: The number of chain isomers possible for the hydrocarbon with molecular formula C$_5$H$_{12}$ is
questions.explanation: C$_5$H$_{12}$ has three chain isomers: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane) and neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane).

questions.q: The compound with molecular formula C$_{20}$H$_{42}$ is
questions.explanation: An alkane C$_n$H$_{2n+2}$ with n = 20 is eicosane, C$_{20}$H$_{42}$.

questions.q: C-Cl bond in methyl chloride compared to C-Cl bond in chlorobenzene is
questions.explanation: In chlorobenzene, resonance gives the C-Cl bond partial double-bond character, making it shorter and stronger than the pure single C-Cl bond in methyl chloride; so methyl chloride's bond is comparatively longer and weaker.

questions.q: The compound from which chlorobenzene cannot be prepared easily is
questions.explanation: Phenol's C-OH bond has partial double-bond character and resists nucleophilic substitution, so it cannot easily be converted to chlorobenzene, unlike benzene (direct chlorination), aniline or benzenediazonium chloride (via Sandmeyer reaction).

questions.q: In S$_N$1 reaction, the alkyl halide that on hydrolysis produces racemic mixture is
questions.explanation: 2-Bromobutane has a chiral centre; S$_N$1 hydrolysis proceeds via a planar carbocation attacked equally from both faces, giving a racemic mixture. The other alkyl halides listed are achiral at the reacting carbon.

questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Chloramphenicol treats typhoid fever, thyroxine deficiency causes goiter, chloroquine is antimalarial, and chloroform is used as an anesthetic.
